lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Skill model: rehearsing the full application sequence

objective: Learners rehearse the full, unbroken application sequence with a trusted adult, from a brief self-introduction through five interview questions to a closing question and thank-you, so they experience the whole sequence together rather than as isolated practiced pieces.
scenario: A trusted adult plays interviewer for the capstone's full practice interview: the learner delivers a short self-introduction, answers five interview questions out loud without a script, asks one closing question, and closes with a thank-you, all in one continuous run-through, then the adult gives feedback on the sequence as a whole.
safetyNotes: No audio or video recording is made; the adult gives feedback live and the learner writes notes afterward.
This is a rehearsal of the sequence, not a real evaluation of the learner's worth; feedback should stay specific to the delivery.

simulationAlternative.description: If no adult is available to play interviewer at this time, the learner instead writes out the full sequence as a script from introduction to closing thank-you, then reads it aloud once to themselves and self-checks it against the same look-fors a live interviewer would use.

materials: five interview questions and notes from earlier this year
paper or notes app for planning and post-interview notes

tasks.directions: Plan your self-introduction (30-45 seconds) and choose your closing question before beginning.

prompts.text: Draft your self-introduction and your closing question.

tasks.directions: With your adult, run the full sequence in one continuous pass: introduction, five questions, closing question, thank-you.

prompts.text: I completed the full sequence in one continuous pass without stopping to restart.
I asked my closing question and thanked the interviewer to close.
My adult gave feedback on the sequence as a whole, not just individual answers.

tasks.directions: Right after, write down the feedback on the sequence as a whole.

prompts.text: Summarize the feedback on how the full sequence flowed, not just individual answers, and name one specific transition you'd smooth out next time.

tasks.directions: Reflect on the difference between practicing pieces and running the whole sequence.

prompts.text: What was different about running the whole sequence together compared to practicing individual pieces earlier this year?

remediation: If a learner's introduction and answers feel disconnected, with awkward stops between each part, reteach by having them practice just the three transition moments (intro-to-first-answer, last-answer-to-closing-question, closing-question-to-thank-you) in isolation, then re-run the full sequence.
extension: Have the learner run the full sequence a second time with one question swapped for a harder one, and compare how the transitions held up under a less familiar question.
